name: Tressette
description: Tressette is one of the great Italian card games. It is a partnership trick-taking game for 4 players using a 40-card Italian deck. The unique ranking (3-2-A high) and the lack of trumps create a pure suit-following game where communication and memory are paramount. There are 11 points per deal.

content.text: Tressette is one of the great Italian card games. It is a partnership trick-taking game for 4 players using a 40-card Italian deck. The unique ranking (3-2-A high) and the lack of trumps create a pure suit-following game where communication and memory are paramount. There are 11 points per deal.

Tressette originated in Italy and is first recorded from the early 18th century; its lack of trumps suggests it may be older. It is one of Italy's major national card games alongside Scopa and Briscola. The name may derive from "Tre Sett" (three sevens): Cäsar (1800) states that a player holding three sevens could declare and win. The game spread to former Italian-influenced regions including Albania, Montenegro, coastal Slovenia and Croatia, and the Canton of Ticino; the Austrian game Trischettn in South Tyrol is a derivative.

items.text: Tressette con la Chiamata del Tre: Partnerships determined by player right of dealer calling a three.
Spizzichino (Tressette in Due): Two-player variant of Tressette.
Terziglio (Calabresella): Three-player variant with bidding; one player versus two on each deal.
